change_1.name: Chang'e-1
change_1.primary_objectives: Global 3D lunar stereoscopic imaging, distribution and abundance of 14 chemical elements, lunar regolith thickness, Earth-Moon space environment.

instruments.name: Laser Altimeter
instruments.description: Global Lunar DEM mapping

instruments.name: Gamma-Ray Spectrometer
instruments.description: Mapping U, Th, K, Fe, Ti, Si, Al, Mg

instruments.name: X-Ray Spectrometer
instruments.description: Fluorescent X-ray detection of Mg, Al, Si

instruments.name: Microwave Radiometer
instruments.description: Global brightness temperature and regolith thickness

instruments.name: Solar Wind Ion Detector
instruments.description: Solar wind interaction with Moon

instruments.name: High-Energy Particle Detector
instruments.description: Cosmic rays and energetic particles

key_discoveries: Produced 120m full-coverage global lunar optical mosaic
Constructed first global high-precision lunar microwave brightness temperature map (CELMS)
Estimated global lunar regolith thickness and Helium-3 inventory

change_2.name: Chang'e-2
change_2.primary_objectives: High-resolution lunar landing site imaging (7m/1.3m), Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point exploration, asteroid Toutatis flyby.

instruments.name: X-Ray / Gamma-Ray Spectrometer
instruments.description: Enhanced resolution elemental mapping

instruments.name: Solar Wind Ion Detector
instruments.description: Solar wind & Lagrange point environment

key_discoveries: Full-moon 7-meter resolution global map (highest resolution global lunar map of its era)
Closest flyby imaging of near-Earth asteroid (4179) Toutatis at 3.2 km distance, revealing bifurcated contact binary structure

change_3.name: Chang'e-3

landing_site.name: Mare Imbrium (Zi Wei Crater / Guang Han Gong)

instruments.name: Lunar Penetrating Radar
instruments.description: Subsurface regolith and basalt layer profiling

instruments.name: Visible and Near-Infrared Spectrometer
instruments.description: In-situ mineral composition and olivine/pyroxene absorption

instruments.name: Active Particle-induced X-ray Spectrometer
instruments.description: In-situ rock and regolith elemental abundances (Mg, Al, Si, K, Ca, Ti, Fe)

instruments.name: Moon-based Ultraviolet Telescope
instruments.description: First long-term UV observatory operating from the lunar surface

instruments.name: Extreme Ultraviolet Camera
instruments.description: Direct global imaging of Earth's plasmasphere

key_discoveries: Identified a new type of lunar basalt with intermediate titanium (TiO2) and high iron (FeO) content
First ground-truth radar stratigraphy down to 400m in Mare Imbrium showing multiple episodic volcanic flooding layers
Continuous astronomical observation from the Moon with LUT (photometry of binary stars and AGN)

change_4.name: Chang'e-4

landing_site.name: Von Kármán Crater, South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin
landing_site.geological_unit: SPA Basin interior / Finsen crater ejecta sheet

rover.name: Yutu-2 (Jade Rabbit-2)
rover.operational_status: Active (World record longevity for lunar rover >5 years)

instruments.name: Lunar Penetrating Radar
instruments.description: Farside regolith stratigraphy & buried craters

instruments.name: Visible and Near-Infrared Spectrometer
instruments.description: Deep mantle mineralogy (low-Ca pyroxene, olivine)

instruments.name: Panoramic Camera
instruments.description: 3D terrain reconstructions & boulder morphology

instruments.name: Lunar Lander Neutrons and Dosimetry
instruments.description: Lunar surface radiation dose equivalent (1369 µSv/day)

instruments.name: Advanced Small Analyzer for Neutrals
instruments.description: Energetic neutral atoms & solar wind sputtering

instruments.name: Low Frequency Radio Spectrometer
instruments.description: Electromagnetically quiet farside cosmic dark age exploration

key_discoveries: First landing and rover exploration on the lunar farside in human history
Discovered low-calcium pyroxene and olivine minerals excavated from the lunar upper mantle by SPA giant impact
Unveiled ~40m thickness of multi-layered porous impact ejecta deposits with low radar attenuation
Precise measurement of lunar surface radiation dose rate for future astronaut safety (60 µSv/h, ~200x Earth surface)

change_5.name: Chang'e-5
change_5.type: Lunar Sample Return (Orbiter, Lander, Ascender, Returner)

landing_site.name: Northern Oceanus Procellarum (Mons Rümker region / Statio Tianchuan)

instruments.name: Lunar Mineralogical Spectrometer
instruments.description: In-situ hydroxyl (OH) and water absorption at 2.85 µm

instruments.name: Lunar Regolith Penetrating Radar
instruments.description: Drill site structural integrity & depth mapping (0 - 2.5m)

instruments.name: Panoramic Camera
instruments.description: Drill and scoop site context imaging

instruments.name: Landing Camera
instruments.description: Descent trajectory optical tracking

key_discoveries: Returned youngest known lunar basalts dated at 2.030 ± 0.004 billion years (extending known lunar volcanic activity by ~1 billion years)
In-situ spectral detection of indigenous water/hydroxyl (OH) in lunar soil (<120 ppm) and apatite crystals (up to 900 ppm)
Identified a new mineral species: Changesite-(Y) (a phosphate mineral in columnar crystals)

change_6.name: Chang'e-6
change_6.type: Lunar Farside Sample Return (Orbiter, Lander, Ascender, Returner)

landing_site.name: Apollo Basin, South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin (Statio Tianhe)

instruments.name: Lunar Mineralogical Spectrometer
instruments.description: In-situ farside mineral & hydration mapping

instruments.name: Lunar Regolith Penetrating Radar
instruments.description: Drill core structure verification

instruments.name: Detection of Outgassing RadoN
instruments.description: Radon outgassing & lunar exosphere dynamics

instruments.name: Negative Ions on Lunar Surface
instruments.description: First detection of negative ions on the Moon from solar wind interaction

key_discoveries: World's first sample return from the lunar farside (1,935.3 g)
Revealed distinct dichotomy in basalt mantle source composition between lunar nearside and farside (low-Ti, depleted in KREEP elements)
First in-situ detection of lunar surface negative ions (NILS)

tianwen_1.name: Tianwen-1 & Zhurong Rover

landing_site.name: Southern Utopia Planitia
landing_site.geological_unit: Vastitas Borealis Formation / Ancient Martian Ocean Basin

instruments.name: Rover Subsurface Penetrating Radar
instruments.description: Subsurface sedimentary & paleoflood stratigraphy

instruments.name: Mars Surface Composition Detector
instruments.type: Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) + Micro-Imager + SWIR (0.85 - 2.4 µm)
instruments.description: Active laser ablation elemental chemistry (Fe, Ti, Si, Mg, Ca, Na, K, H, O)

instruments.name: Multispectral Camera
instruments.description: Rock color ratios and iron oxidation

instruments.name: Navigation and Terrain Camera
instruments.description: Traverse routing and digital elevation modeling

instruments.name: Mars Rover Magnetometer
instruments.description: Surface remanent crustal magnetic field

instruments.name: Mars Climate Station
instruments.description: Martian boundary layer dynamics

key_discoveries: Discovered multi-layered paleoflood sedimentary units within top 80m of Utopia Planitia beneath fine duricrust
Identified hydrated sulfate minerals (gypsum, bassanite) in Amazonian-aged duricrust, indicating persistent liquid water activity in Mars's recent geological epoch (<1 Ga)
Discovered 16 buried polygon structures forming an ancient wet thermal-contraction cracked paleolandscape
Captured high-fidelity sound recordings of Martian wind and rover mobility
